title: Think, pair, share
keyIdea: Think, pair, share is a way to answer a big question. Think: on your own, quietly, find an idea and a reason. Pair: take turns with a partner. One talks while the other listens, then swap. Share: tell the class what you both think, starting "We think…" and giving a reason with "because". The quiet think time first means everyone gets an idea, not just the fastest few.
familyTip: Try it at dinner. Ask a question such as "What would make a good school trip?", then say "Think first, no talking!" and wait a few seconds. Take turns to tell each other your idea. Then ask your child to tell everyone "We think… because…", using both ideas.

visual.caption: Is it think time, pair time or share time? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: Find an idea and a reason
Say back what my partner said

lab.caption: Flagship lab: drag a think timer, fill a think bubble, take turns with Mia, build a share sentence, then put the steps in order.

kid: The teacher asks a big question. First, think. Keep quiet and find your own idea. Then find a reason: because…
Next, pair. Talk with a friend. Take turns. When your friend talks, you listen. Can you say their idea back?
Last, share. Tell the class what you both think. Start with "We think…" and give a reason.
Why think first? Some of us need more time to have an idea. A few quiet seconds let everyone get one.
adult: Ages 6 to 7. Think, pair, share was set out by Frank Lyman (1981) as a way to get every child in a class thinking and talking, not only the few who put a hand up first. It fits the Key Stage 1 spoken language goals in the National Curriculum (2014): listen and respond, give and justify answers, and take turns in discussion.

Each step has a job. Think gives quiet time to form an idea and a reason. Pair lets the child try the idea out loud in a safe space, and hear another view. Share asks the pair to speak for both of them. Mary Budd Rowe found that when teachers wait about 3 seconds or more after a question, more children answer and their answers get longer. The EEF rates structured talk as a high-impact, low-cost approach.

Common mistakes: answering at once, so only the fastest get to think; copying a partner and skipping the think; one child keeping the turn; planning your next point and not listening; sharing only your own idea; giving no reason; and calling a partner's idea silly. Be careful not to cut the think time short. A few quiet seconds can feel long, but they matter.

In the lab your child drags a think timer and watches how many children in a made-up class have an idea. Then they fill a think bubble with an idea and a reason, and take turns with Mia, saying her idea back. Next they build a "We think… because…" sentence that uses both ideas. Last, they put think, pair and share in order.

practice.prompt: The teacher asks a question. What do you do first?
practice.explain: Think comes first. Quiet think time lets you find your own idea.

practice.prompt: You and your partner each have {n} turns to talk. How many turns in all?
practice.hint: There are 2 of you. Add your turns and your partner's turns.
practice.explain: {n} turns each for 2 people makes {=2*n} turns.

practice.prompt: Your partner is talking. What should you do?
practice.hint: Can you say their idea back after?
practice.explain: Listen, so you can say their idea back. Then it is your turn.

practice.prompt: {n} pairs share with the class. Each pair has 2 children. How many children is that?
practice.hint: Count in twos, once for each pair.

practice.prompt: How do you start your share?
practice.hint: You are speaking for you and your partner.
practice.explain: Start with "We think…", because you share what both of you said.

pool.prompt: Why does the teacher wait before hands go up?
choices: So everyone has time to think
pool.hint: Does everyone get an idea at the same speed?
pool.explain: Some children need more seconds to have an idea. Waiting lets everyone think.

pool.prompt: What goes in your think bubble?
choices: My own idea and a reason
pool.hint: Think time is for your own idea.
pool.explain: Your own idea, with a reason such as "because the sun melts snow".

pool.prompt: You said your idea. What do you do next?
pool.hint: Pairs take turns: one talks, one listens. Whose turn is it now?
pool.explain: Pass the turn. Your partner talks and you listen.

pool.prompt: Mia says, "Make it big." What shows you listened?
pool.hint: Say back what Mia said, not your idea.
pool.explain: Saying her idea back shows you listened. Shade was your own idea.

pool.prompt: The teacher waits {n} seconds. Then she waits 2 more seconds. How many seconds of think time?
pool.hint: Start at the first number and count on 2.
pool.explain: {n} seconds and 2 more make {=n+2} seconds of think time.

choices: We think it should be big, because big ones melt slower
pool.hint: Look for both an idea and a reason.
pool.explain: A good share gives the idea and a reason with because.

pool.hint: What must you do before you talk?
pool.explain: Think first, then pair, then share.

pool.prompt: {n} pairs are in the class. 1 more pair joins. How many pairs now?
pool.hint: Count the pairs, then one more.

pool.prompt: Your idea and Mia's idea are not the same. What do you share?
pool.hint: You share what the pair thinks.
pool.explain: Share both. "We think… and also…" tells the class both ideas.
